'''Bruce Carl Berndt''' (born March 13, 1939) 
is an American [[mathematician]]. Berndt attended college at [[Albion College]], graduating in 1961, where he also ran track. He received his master's and [[doctorate|doctoral]] degrees from the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]]. He lectured for a year at the [[University of Glasgow]] and then, in 1967, was appointed an assistant professor at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]], where he has remained since. In 1973–74, he was a visiting scholar at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in Princeton.<ref>[https://www.ias.edu/people/cos/users/4033 Berndt, Bruce Carl | Institute for Advanced Study]</ref> He is currently ({{As of|2006|lc=on}}) [[Michio Suzuki (mathematician)|Michio Suzuki]] Distinguished Research Professor of Mathematics at the University of Illinois.{{Update inline|date=August 2026|reason=20 years?}}

Berndt is an [[analytic number theory|analytic number theorist]] who is known for his work explicating the discoveries of [[Srinivasa Ramanujan]].<ref name="RamanujanEssays">{{cite book | editor1-first=Bruce C. | editor2-last=Rankin | editor2-first=Robert A.  | editor1-last=Berndt | last=Rankin | title=Ramanujan: Essays and Surveys | publisher=American Mathematical Soc. | publication-place=Providence, Rhode Island | date=2001 | isbn=978-0-8218-2624-9 | doi=10.1090/hmath/022 | url=http://www.ams.org/hmath/022  }}</ref><ref name="Charlemagne">{{cite book | last1=Butzer | first1=Paul Leo | last2=Oberschelp | first2=Walter | title=Karl der Grosse und sein Nachwirken: Mathematisches Wissen | publisher=Brepols | publication-place=Turnhout | date=1998 | isbn=978-2-503-50674-6 | language=de | pages= 119–146}}</ref> He is a coordinating editor of ''[[The Ramanujan Journal]]'' and, in 1996, received an expository [[Steele Prize]] from the [[American Mathematical Society]] for his work editing ''Ramanujan's Notebooks''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://math.nist.gov/opsf/personal/berndt.html|title=Steele Prize for Bruce Berndt|date=15 January 1997|website=OP–SF Net 4.1}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/199611/comm-steele.pdf|title=1996 Steele Prizes|journal=Notices of the AMS|pages=340–347|volume=43|issue=11|date=November 1996}}</ref> A [[Lester R. Ford Award]] was given to Berndt, with Gert Almkvist, in 1989<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Almkvist, Gert|author2=Berndt, Bruce C.|title=Gauss, Landen, Ramanujan, the arithmetic-geometric mean, ellipses, π and the Ladies Diary|journal=Amer. Math. Monthly|volume=95|issue=7|year=1988|pages=585–608|url=http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/gauss-landen-ramanujan-the-arithmetic-geometric-mean-ellipses-pi-and-the-ladies-diary|doi=10.2307/2323302|jstor=2323302|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and to Berndt, with S. Bhargava, in 1994.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Berndt, Bruce C.|author2=Bhargava, S.|title=Ramanujan—for lowbrows|journal=Amer. Math. Monthly|volume=100|issue=7|year=1993|pages=644–656|url=http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/ramanujan-for-lowbrows|doi=10.2307/2323885|jstor=2323885|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-10.</ref>
In December 2012, he received an honorary doctorate<ref>[http://lists.siam.org/pipermail/siam-opsf/2013-January/000077.html Honorary doctorates for Andrews, Askey and Berndt]</ref> from [[SASTRA University]] in [[Kumbakonam]], India.
